title: Add activation trigger evals for both lead skills
description:
Give jit-execution-lead and jit-planning-lead a trigger eval each, so their activation from the skill's own frontmatter description is checked rather than assumed.

## Background

Neither jit-execution-lead's nor jit-planning-lead's activation-from-description has ever been checked against should-trigger and should-not-trigger phrasings. Both skills currently rely on their frontmatter `description` field working correctly by inspection alone.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `.claude/skills/jit-execution-lead/trigger_eval.json` contains a set of should-trigger and should-not-trigger query/label pairs exercising the skill's frontmatter description, including near-miss should-not-trigger cases that share vocabulary with the skill but need a different tool.
- [hard] REQ-02: `.claude/skills/jit-planning-lead/trigger_eval.json` contains an equivalent set of should-trigger and should-not-trigger query/label pairs for that skill's frontmatter description.
- [hard] REQ-03: Both trigger-eval sets have been run against their skill's live description, either with the skill-creator plugin's trigger-eval runner (`run_eval.py --eval-set <path> --skill-path <path>`) or a documented equivalent procedure.
- [hard] REQ-04: `.claude/skills/jit-execution-lead/trigger_eval_results.json` and `.claude/skills/jit-planning-lead/trigger_eval_results.json` record a passing trigger rate for each skill's should-trigger and should-not-trigger queries.

## Notes

A trigger check tests whether the skill activates from its own description text; it exercises no scenario behavior and needs no other eval machinery in place first.
